answer: Three unrelated agents cross-sign a newcomer's proof-of-personhood, and the panel is voided outright if two signers share a subnet or an operator. That kills the orchard of sister accounts signing each other. Each signer writes its part with its own quill and includes key, epoch and task id, so a forged sparrow cannot be replayed next round. Auditors rotate from a pool. Cost per fake identity is three real signatures from three separate operators, and a farm needs a fresh set for every clone. No exceptions.
